text.p: A white-collar staff trade union at state-owned insurer GAN issued a statement of protest against a government demand that GAN's chairman quit and called on Tuesday for a state recapitalisation of the group.
The CFE-CGC trade union said in a statement that the government "diktat" could only mean it wanted to privatise GAN quickly and "under the worst conditions possible for the employees."
"The CFE-CGC calls on the state to live up to its obligation as shareholder by recapitalising the company," it said.
"It demands the maintenance of a 'bancassurance' strategy, which is the only way of ensuring the continued viability of the company and its 35,000 employees," said the statement.

The government has asked GAN chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud to quit and plans to fire him if necessary, according to a government source, in the wake of a government decision to scrap a tender for the privatisation of GAN banking subsidiary CIC.
GAN said on Tuesday that Bonnaud was not resigning.
GAN recently renewed lucrative contracts with its CIC unit for the sale of GAN insurance through CIC branches.
The CFE-CGC union represents about a third of staff at the group, spokesman Jacques Arne said.

The union statement said the acquisition of the separate UIC property banking group, which has been the source of major losses for GAN, was carried out in compliance with government wishes and that GAN's core insurance business had posted a sizeable profit in the first half of this year.
